text:
sahil: Heads up — CI microbench failed on PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12890, threshold delta +12% on kv_cache_hit_rate test :sob:

maria: saw that, failing perf unit not flaky?

sahil: looks consistent across 3 re-runs in CI, attaching the diff from the runner log and bench summary

maria: can you paste the bench snippet?

sahil: ```
bench.kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline 0.842 -> pr 0.740 (delta -0.102, -12.1%)
bench.prefetch_batch_latency_p50: baseline 3.2ms -> pr 3.6ms (delta +12.5%)
kernel_selector: chosen nv_fused_attention_v2 -> nv_attention_opt_v1
```

lee: interesting, kernel switch + kv hit drop. PR touches batch sampler heuristics and kernel hinting in autoselect right?

priya: correct, PR updates the batching priority so short sequences are batched differently and adds a soft hint for kernel selection when seq_len < 64

maria: might be an interaction where the new batching increases prefix cache churn causing kv hit rate to drop. if kernel hint changed, maybe the fallback path has worse cache locality.

perf-bot: bisect started: suspect range 0a1f3c..ef4b2a, running microbench suite on 8 seeds

sahil: local repro steps I ran:
```
# run microbench locally with golden models
pytest tests/perf/test_kv_cache.py::test_kv_cache_hit_rate -k kv_cache_hit_rate -q --runs 5
python tools/run_bench.py --model redwood-34b --seq-len 32 --seed 42
```

lee: can you attach perf profile (nvprof/timestamp)? want to see kernel runtime split and memcpy hotspots

sahil: attached short perf output (summarized):
```
NV Kernel: nv_attention_opt_v1  74% token-time
KV Cache memcpy H2D -> 18% (increased vs baseline 5%)
Small-kernel launch overhead increased by ~30us per batch
```

priya: H2D memcpy spike screams batching change — maybe more small batches hitting copy instead of pipelined batched memcpy. The kernel autoselect hint might force a kernel variant that expects contiguous KV layout.

maria: can we reproduce with the old batching policy but new kernel hint to isolate?

lee: I'll run two quick CI-like runs: (1) new PR but force old batch_sampler config, (2) new PR but disable kernel hint. posting results in a few mins

perf-bot: bisect update: commit 0f3a7d introduced batch sampler reorder, commit b2e9c1 changed kernel hint weights

lee: run1 (force old sampler): kv_hit_rate -> 0.838 (close to baseline), p50 latency 3.3ms
lee: run2 (disable kernel hint): kv_hit_rate -> 0.736, p50 3.6ms

maria: so sampler reorder is the main regression vector, kernel hint amplifies it but isn't the root cause.

sahil: good. we should revert the sampler change in this PR and re-land kernel hint separately with improved tests. can we do a targeted revert commit to unblock the rollout?

priya: I can open a follow-up that reverts the sampler reorder and adds a golden perf test exercising small-seq batching + kv cache telemetry.

maria: agree. also add a unit test asserting that kv_cache_hit_rate doesn't drop >3% across sampler configs in CI smoke.

deploy-bot: deploy paused for PR 12890 due to perf regression alert (policy: block_on_perf_threshold).

lee: opening a quick revert PR now and will trigger CI. cc @sahil @maria

sahil: thanks — once revert passes microbench I'll merge and then we can iterate on kernel hint separately with more telemetry.

priya: filing follow-up issue: PERF-3492 "Sampler reorder interacts with KV layout causing increased H2D copies" with repro steps and perf traces.

maria: note for postmortem: add test coverage for kernel_autoselect hint + sampler combo, and add a perf unit that runs on small cloud worker with seq_len distribution matching product traffic.

lee: CI revert PR passed microbench, merging revert. will keep an eye on rollout.

sahil: thanks all. marking this thread as resolved for now, will reopen if we see noise after next merge. :thumbsup:
